data.title: Google releases new Gemini models built to improve conversing capabilities of voice agents
data.description:
Google (GOOG)(GOOGL) released a pair of new Gemini models on Tuesday, 3.8 Live and 3.8 Live Extended Thinking, which were designed to improve the capabilities of voice agents.

"For developers and enterprises, these models deliver the building blocks for reliable, production-ready voice agents," said Google engineer Tom Ouyang in a blog post. "They also make speaking with Gemini across the Gemini app, Google Workspace, and Search more fluid and collaborative—helping you tackle complex tasks using just your voice."

Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking scored an 82.6% on the Artificial Intelligence Speech to Speech Index. It just outperformed OpenAI's (OPENAI) GPT-Live-1 Astra, which scored an 81.5%, and SpaceXAI's (SPCX) Grok Voice Think Fast 2.0, which scored an 81.3%.

"For tasks that require deeper reasoning, 3.8 Live Extended Thinking reasons and speaks simultaneously," Ouyang said. "It delivers increased intelligence for complex workflows while maintaining an uninterrupted conversational flow—using early verbal cues like 'Let me check that…' to acknowledge prompts naturally, and live progress narration to walk users through multi-step background tasks as they progress."

Google is also partnering with Salesforce (CRM), Genspark and Lumeris on use cases for the new models.

"By bringing together real-time, multimodal capabilities with agentic AI, we're exploring new ways to create richer, more intuitive customer experiences from first contact to resolution," said Bob Van Osten, vice president of Product for Agentforce at Salesforce.

Gemini 3.8 Live is available today for developers in the Gemini API and Google AI Studio, in private preview in Gemini Enterprise and for all users in Search Live. Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking is available today for developers in the Gemini API and Google AI Studio, in private preview for enterprises in Gemini Enterprise and for all users in Gemini Live and Google AI Pro.

data.title: Middleby rises after J.P. Morgan upgrade cites earnings, margin potential
data.description:
Middleby (MIDD) shares climbed as much as 3.8% after J.P. Morgan upgraded the commercial cooking-equipment maker to Overweight from Neutral, citing the potential for stronger earnings and a higher valuation. The S&P 500 (SP500) was negative for the day.

Analyst Tami Zakaria said Middleby (MIDD) could benefit as management works to accelerate growth and improve profitability following the spinoff of Midera Food Processing.

Middleby’s stock had been under pressure since July. Zakaria attributed the decline partly to disappointing second-quarter margins. Some event-driven investors also reduced or closed their positions after the Midera separation.

Those factors may create an opportunity for longer-term investors. J.P. Morgan expects margins to recover during the coming quarters as price increases and cost reductions take effect.

The firm also sees relatively modest expectations for the second half of 2026. That could make it easier for Middleby to meet its forecasts or deliver better-than-anticipated results.

J.P. Morgan set a December 2027 price target of $147. Its previous target was $141 for December 2026. The new target represents about 34% upside from Middleby’s latest closing price.

Middleby on Sept. 9 reaffirmed its full-year forecast for adjusted earnings of $6.73 to $6.89 a share on revenue of $2.48 billion to $2.53 billion. The company also maintained third-quarter guidance for earnings of $1.67 to $1.83 a share and revenue of $620 million to $640 million.

For investors, the upgrade rests on the view that Middleby’s (MIDD) recent weakness reflects temporary margin pressure and post-spinoff selling rather than a lasting deterioration in its business. The main test will be whether pricing actions and cost savings produce the expected improvement while the streamlined company delivers on its 2026 guidance.

data.title: Hot money or structural shift? Inside the emerging market debt surge
data.description:
Emerging market (EEM) debt issuance is on track to break records for the second consecutive year, fueled by sustained economic growth, substantial refinancing requirements and a surge in investor demand for portfolio diversification, according to Stefan Weiler, head of CEEMEA Debt Capital Markets at J.P. Morgan.

Since 2022, when issuance totaled some $110B, volumes have climbed steadily each year, with 2026 poised to surpass last year's historic highs, Weiler told CNBC in an interview.

The current wave of capital flowing into emerging markets marks a notable departure from past boom-bust cycles. Unlike the hot-money dynamics that contributed to the late-1990s Asian financial crisis, today's inflows appear structural rather than opportunistic, Weiler contended.

Emerging markets have attracted net inflows for 16 consecutive months—excluding a brief disruption in March tied to geopolitical tensions—with anticipated inflows of $40B to $50B this year. Spreads remain near historic lows, yet investor appetite shows few signs of weakening, the strategist said.

African (AFK) sovereigns have emerged as standout performers, with Nigeria and Angola drawing increased attention as investors seek alternatives to traditional Middle Eastern oil exporters, Weiler noted. At the same time, many emerging market governments are diversifying their funding strategies by issuing more debt in local and niche currencies to reduce exposure to U.S. dollar (DXY) volatility.

Macro dynamics may provide an additional tailwind. According to J.P. Morgan Asset Management, if the Federal Reserve continues to hold rates steady while other central banks tighten, narrowing short-term yield differentials could strengthen foreign currencies against the dollar—a potential boost for international equities and emerging market assets alike.

data.title: Iran war costs reach $38B as inflation, supply risks mount
data.description:
The war with Iran cost U.S. taxpayers about $38 billion during its first five months and is expected to add to inflation, according to a new Congressional Budget Office analysis.

The estimate covers replacement weapons, equipment lost in combat, additional flight operations and higher fuel expenses. It is close to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s July estimate of $37.5 billion.

The CBO said the conflict could cost another $2 billion to $3 billion for each additional month. Expenses could rise faster if fighting intensifies.

For investors, the report points to continued demand for defense equipment while raising concerns about interest rates and consumer spending. Higher energy costs could keep inflation above the Federal Reserve’s preferred path, potentially delaying rate cuts. Defense contractors may benefit from efforts to replenish weapons stockpiles, though federal funding remains subject to congressional approval.

Inflation pressure builds

Disruptions to oil and gas shipments through the Strait of Hormuz are expected to lift a key inflation gauge by about half a percentage point in early 2027 compared with the CBO’s February forecast.

Core personal consumption expenditures inflation, which excludes food and energy, is projected to be 0.3 percentage point higher. The CBO expects those underlying price pressures to emerge more slowly but persist longer.

That outlook could complicate the Federal Reserve’s policy decisions. A sustained increase in core inflation may reduce the central bank’s flexibility to lower interest rates even if economic growth weakens.

Weapons inventories face lengthy recovery

The fighting has also reduced U.S. munitions inventories. Rebuilding some stockpiles could take five years or more, according to the CBO.

The shortage may limit the military’s ability to respond to another large conflict, particularly one involving extensive use of ballistic and cruise missiles. The report identified a potential China-Taiwan conflict as one scenario in which those constraints could become significant.

A separate assessment by the Pentagon’s inspector general reportedly found that the defense industry cannot currently replace munitions as quickly as they are being consumed.

Trump has disputed concerns about shortages, saying the United States has ample ammunition.

Congress weighs additional funding

House Republicans advanced a budget plan in July that would provide $73 billion to the military and intelligence agencies for Iran-related expenses. The proposal has stalled in the Senate and may not receive consideration until after the Nov. 3 midterm elections.

Lawmakers are also considering a separate $350 billion increase in mandatory Pentagon spending. Part of that package would be financed through efforts to reduce healthcare fraud.

The two proposals could be combined after the election. Trump, who said in March that the conflict was nearly finished, has since acknowledged that it could continue beyond Election Day.

data.title: Autodesk initiated with Neutral rating due to near-term AI concerns: Cantor
data.description:
Cantor initiated coverage on Autodesk (ADSK) with a Neutral rating, as the financial services firm believes the rise of artificial intelligence poses a credible threat to the design software stalwart.

"ADSK is the global leader in Design software, with strong franchises in AutoCAD, Revit, Fusion, Civil 3D, Inventor, and Forma," said Cantor analyst Mason Marion in an in-depth investor report. "While AI poses perhaps the most credible threat to these franchises in ADSK's history, we expect the company to endure and grow in the AI era."

"ADSK is not standing by idly, investing in proprietary 3D generative AI models (neural CAD) and infusing Autodesk AI throughout its platform," he added. "Outside of Design, ADSK is leveraging its strong Design franchises to expand into Construction with Forma for Construction ($600m+ TTM rev growing 20%+)."

In addition, Autodesk's recent $3.6B acquisition of MaintainX is expected to increase its total addressable market.

Cantor set a price target of $215 on Autodesk, as it believes the market has already established a fair value for the stock.

data.title: FuelCell Energy started with Neutral rating at Citi as product backlog remains modest
data.description:
FuelCell Energy (FCEL) falls 0.9% in Tuesday's trading as Citi initiated coverage with a Neutral rating and $19 price target, noting progress towards strategic and financial objectives is picking up pace, with demand from hyperscaler data centers and colocation/neocloud providers driving the order pipeline to ~10 GW, and average proposal sizes rising ~3x over the last six months.

The company offers several differentiated strengths, according to Citi's Vikram Bagri, including native DC baseload power, rapid deployment timelines, and more than 20 years of utility-scaleoperating experience, while its molten carbonate platform benefits from a largely U.S.-based supply chain, improved seven-year stack life, better power density, low emissions, chilled-water production, and carbon-capture capabilities.

To leverage the technology and position FuelCell (FCEL) for long-term success, Bagri said management has implemented recent restructurings that should allow operating expenses to grow roughly in line with inflation while the company benefits from strong operating leverage as it grows production and achieves positive adjusted EBITDA in Q4 2027.

However, FuelCell's (FCEL) product backlog remains modest at ~$109M, and the broader pipeline has yet to convert meaningfully into firm orders, and its ~50% efficiency trails Bloom Energy's SOFC platform, while expanding gas turbine, fuel cell, and engine manufacturing capacity could increase competitive pressure, the analyst said.

data.title: Boeing is said to near deal with Turkish Airlines for 150 737 Max jets
data.description:
Boeing (BA) is nearing an agreement to sell 150 737 Max jets to Turkish Airlines after a dispute over engine maintenance delayed the order, Reuters reported Tuesday, citing people familiar with the negotiations.

The purchase is part of a broader agreement for 225 Boeing (BA) aircraft announced after Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan met U.S. President Donald Trump last year. The Max portion could be finalized as soon as next week.

Turkish Airlines had threatened to switch the order to Airbus amid disagreements with engine manufacturer CFM International over maintenance costs, spare-parts prices and long-term repair risks. CFM is jointly owned by GE Aerospace (GE) and Safran (SAFRF)(SAFRY).

The carrier also sought a leading role in CFM’s maintenance network, which would give it faster access to repair technology for engines used on the 737 Max. It remains unclear whether that request will be included in the final agreement.

A completed order would preserve one of the major Boeing agreements announced by the White House last year. Turkish media have reported that Trump and Erdogan may meet during United Nations gatherings in New York next week.

Turkish Airlines operates more than 400 Boeing and Airbus aircraft. It is also considering regional jets from Embraer and Airbus as well as the larger Boeing 777X and Airbus A350-1000 as it expands its Istanbul hub.

data.title: Hedgeye reiterates RadNet long idea
data.description:
Hedgeye is reiterating its long call on RadNet (RDNT) with the potential for 30% upside.

"The valuation looks stretched against consensus, but we can model upside well into 2027 on several simultaneous secular tailwinds that justify the premium: (1) continued inpatient-to-outpatient imaging migration, (2) mix shift toward high-margin advanced imaging (PET/CT, MRI, and CT), where both volumes and pricing are accelerating on demand from Alzheimer's, Oncology, and Cardiology, and (3) AI tailwinds driving incremental revenue and operating leverage," Hedgeye analyst Tom Tobin wrote in a note.

"Our model puts 2027 total Adj. EBITDA at $500M versus the Street at $421M, roughly 19% ahead. Even into the Q3 2026 print we sit above consensus, at $104M versus the Street's $95M," Tobin added.

Shares of RadNet (RDNT) rose 3.8% on Tuesday and have gained 5.8% this year. 

RadNet (RDNT) is set to present at the Morgan Stanley 24th Annual Global Healthcare conferece in New York on Wednesday.

data.title: West Fraser raised at Raymond James as 'housing recovery not necessary to buy the trees'
data.description:
West Fraser Timber (WFG) gains 2.1% in Tuesday's trading as Raymond James upgraded the wood products company to Outperform from Market Perform with an $85 price target, which also raised Interfor (IFSPF) and Canfor (CFPZF) to Strong Buy, saying a U.S. housing recovery is "not necessary to buy the trees."

After four years of depressed U.S. housing, repair, and renovation activity, Raymond James analyst Daryl Swetlishoff said the supply side "has finally done the heavy lifting to improve balance in North American lumber markets," Canadian shipments have fallen to record lows, capacity has permanently exited the system, and European lumber imports have fallen sharply.

Despite cyclical and seasonal demand headwinds, 2026 results approached "what we consider mid-cycle profitability with our refreshed 3Q26 estimates not too far behind," the analyst wrote.

With lumber equities still trading at or below tangible book value, Swetlishoff said a U.S. housing recovery is not currently priced in the stocks, but the analyst "could see ~30% higher benchmark lumber pricing, translating to 100%-300% theoretical equity upside... hence, we see a compelling asymmetric setup with meaningful upside available before underwriting any macro improvement."

"We recommend investors build full positions now as we head into the 2026-27 seasonal trade," the analyst said.

data.title: Soft August dining traffic weighs on restaurant sector
data.description:
Restaurant stocks are on the defensive Tuesday as industry data showed a meaningful decline in dining traffic, albeit largely driven by the timing of this year’s Labor Day weekend.

According to the  August 2026 Retail and Dining Index from Placer.ai, dining visits were down 2.4% in August, reversing a gradual improvement in June and July after a 2.5% decline in May 2026.

Because of the timing of the Labor Day weekend this year, dining activity that would typically begin in late August was pushed into September with the Labor Day holiday falling on September 7 vs. September 1 in 2025.

The survey also attributes the soft dining trends to macroeconomic conditions, as a gallon of gas exceeded $4 per gallon in August, putting 2026 on track as one of the most expensive years for gas.

Dining traffic was down in every state except California, which saw a slight uptick from a year ago. Notable weakness was seen in Montana, Wyoming, South Dakota, New Mexico, Vermont, and West Virginia.

The pressure on the restaurant sector is weighing on the Consumer Discretionary SPDR ETF (XLY) and Vanguard Consumer Discretionary ETF (VCR).
